To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) Neo learns concepts by sensorimotor experience, b) Neo learns concepts without a priori knowledge of categories or concepts, and c) Neo learns concepts that generalize to novel objects, locations and activities.
Neo learns to categorize its environment and to perform general activities, such as walking and reaching, without prior knowledge of physics, geometry and other domain-specific concepts.
Neo can learn concepts from sensorimotor experience, and that Neo can learn classes from these concepts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an agent that learns to interact with its environment, and in the process, learns about the environment.
how an agent can develop an understanding of the world by interacting with it, without relying on prior knowledge of language, or of the world itself.
how an arti cially intelligent agent can acquire conceptual knowledge from sensorimotor interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper presents an approach to conceptual learning which is based on sensorimotor interaction and activity.
Neo has learned the basic concepts of its environment, but it still has much to learn about how to learn.
we can envision a developmental path, but we do not know how to get to the nal goal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how a system can learn a rich, structured representation of its experience, and that it can learn classes of concepts based on that representation.
Neo learns to understand its own actions and the world around it by acting in that world.
we have developed a framework for a new kind of conceptual knowledge that can be acquired through sensorimotor interaction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to learn a fairly accurate representation of the world by sensorimotor interactions, and that this representation can serve as the basis for learning concepts.
a relatively unstructured sensorimotor representation can support learning and abstraction in a way that is compatible with the human conceptual system.
it is possible to learn concepts in an embodied agent without requiring a large amount of prior structure.
